module_title: Important Salts, Chemical Formulas, and Uses
introduction: This is the most memorization-heavy but highly scoring part of the science section. Examiners will directly ask you to match common names to their chemical formulas and uses.

core_concepts.title: Baking Soda
core_concepts.description:
Chemical Name: Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate (or Sodium Bicarbonate). 
Formula: $NaHCO_3$ 
Uses: Used in making baking powder, as an antacid to cure acidity, and in soda-acid fire extinguishers.

core_concepts.title: Washing Soda
core_concepts.description:
Chemical Name: Sodium Carbonate Decahydrate. 
Formula: $Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O$ 
Uses: Used in glass, soap, and paper industries. Used to remove the 'permanent hardness' of water.

core_concepts.title: Bleaching Powder
core_concepts.description:
Chemical Name: Calcium Oxychloride. 
Formula: $CaOCl_2$ 
Uses: Used for disinfecting drinking water (killing germs) and bleaching cotton and linen in the textile industry.

core_concepts.title: Plaster of Paris (POP)
core_concepts.description:
Chemical Name: Calcium Sulfate Hemihydrate. 
Formula: $CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$ 
Preparation: Made by heating 'Gypsum' ($CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$) at exactly $373 K$ ($100^\circ C$). 
Uses: Used by doctors for setting fractured bones, making toys, and decorative ceilings.

important_entities.name: Water of Crystallization
important_entities.significance: Some salt crystals appear perfectly dry but actually contain a fixed number of water molecules chemically bound to them. For example, 'Blue Vitriol' (Copper sulfate) is $CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O$. Upon heating, it loses this water and turns white.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Baking soda is just pure $NaHCO_3$. 'Baking Powder', however, is a physical mixture of Baking Soda and a mild edible acid like 'Tartaric acid'. The tartaric acid is added to neutralize the bitter taste that sodium carbonate would leave in the cake.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Gypsum has '2' waters, POP is 'Half' dry.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Both are calcium sulfates. Gypsum = $CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$. When you heat it, 1.5 molecules evaporate, leaving Plaster of Paris = $CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$.

exam_strategy_tips: Consistently asked in Banking and Railway exams: 'What is the chemical formula of Bleaching Powder?' Answer: $CaOCl_2$.
